'''''Alcantarea imperialis''''' is a robust [[lithophytic]] [[species]] of bromeliad (family [[Bromeliaceae]]) in the genus ''[[Alcantarea]]''.<ref name=":0">{{Cite web|title=''Alcantarea imperialis'' (Carrière) Harms {{!}} Plants of the World Online {{!}} Kew Science|url=http://powo.science.kew.org/taxon/urn:lsid:ipni.org:names:8048-2|access-date=2021-12-08|website=Plants of the World Online|language=en}}</ref> This species is [[Endemism|endemic]] to [[Brazil]].<ref name=":0" />

It was first described in 1888 as ''Vriesea imperialis'' by [[Élie-Abel Carrière]], who dedicated it to the Emperor [[Dom Pedro]] of Brazil with the species epithet, ''imperialis''.<ref>{{cite journal|author=Carrière, E.-A. |date=1888|journal=Revue horticole|location=Paris|volume= 60|pages=58| url=https://www.biodiversitylibrary.org/page/49624132|title=''Vriesia imperialis''}}</ref> It was assigned to the genus, ''[[Alcantarea]]'', by [[Hermann Harms]] in 1930.<ref>Harms, H.A.T. (1930) Die natürlichen Pflanzenfamilien, ed. 2 [Engler & Prantl] 15a: 126</ref>

==Description==
This large terrestrial [[bromeliad]] was once classified as ''[[Vriesea]] imperialis'' but is now recognized as part of the genus ''Alcantarea''. It can be found growing on rocky slopes in the [[Serra dos Órgãos]] in [[Rio de Janeiro]]. It can tolerate dry conditions and full sunlight. Considered one of the giants of the genus, "its leathery leaves measuring 6 inches in width and 5 feet in length."<ref>{{cite book|last=Padilla|first=Victoria|title=Bromeliads|year=1973|publisher=Crown Publishers|location=New York|isbn=0517562413|pages=[https://archive.org/details/bromeliads00vict/page/104 104]|url-access=registration|url=https://archive.org/details/bromeliads00vict/page/104}}</ref>  It will take up to 40 years before producing an imposing red [[inflorescence]] that reaches eight or even {{cvt|3|m|abbr=on}} in height. Its tank will hold up to {{cvt|30|l}} of rainwater.<ref>{{cite journal | last= Martinelli | first= Gustavo | date= March 2000 | title= The Bromeliads of the Atlantic Forest | journal= Scientific American | volume= 282 | issue= 3 | pages= 86–93}}</ref>
